sourceReview.scope: Current unofficial client model, private local-app draft/editor/processor, public app discovery and consented connection, account/backend-scoped setup persistence, retained card compatibility, optional app-declared OCR and private-app handoff/setup. Original upstream onboarding, native sign-in, AuthClient/IdentityStorage and worker bootstrap are restored; retained legacy browser-auth/remembered-session modules remain source-reviewed but are not active sign-in or packaged browser-auth assets. This scope does not enable or require new OpenChat backend canisters.
exclusions: Historical PR1/PR2 inventories and advisory decisions are preserved separately, not accepted as current source snapshots.

Original auth restoration is bounded by exact mixed-file anchors and pinned-upstream comparisons; unrelated core authentication, chat, wallet, media and build dependency imports are not selected merely by coexistence. Retained legacy browser-auth/remembered-session helpers stay in source coverage without claiming active transport.
Mixed entrypoints and build hooks have exact feature ownership anchors; only dedicated feature modules undergo direct-import scanning.
Mixed client/worker/config/sign-in UI and reached account-link/passkey helpers have exact feature anchors and whole-file drift fingerprints, not scans or approval of unrelated core imports.

Private draft recovery is now separately approved device-local encrypted storage using built-in IndexedDB/Web Crypto, account/backend scope, exact request identity, no restored approval/session and no automatic send. It is not chat synchronization, remote pre-review verification or XSS isolation. The existing idb root also covers the retained dormant native remembered-sign-in source, not a new package edge.

Private app setup persistence uses browser IndexedDB and existing catalog, processor-hash and Web Crypto helpers. Only consented connected/imported setup, bounded public installation metadata, selected verified processors and chat opt-ins are saved; messages, drafts, approvals, credentials and handoff payloads are excluded from that setup store. Native remembered sign-in is a distinct approved account/backend-bound store.
Source ownership is not advisory, runtime, image-accuracy, phone, deployment or release acceptance.
